page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn5-c4g1.xlarge is a GPU-accelerated cloud instance powered by 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores on an Intel Xeon E5-2682 v4 processor running at 2.5 GHz. The server includes 30 GB of system RAM, providing 7.5 GB of memory per vCPU core. Compute acceleration is driven by a single dedicated NVIDIA Pascal P100 GPU featuring 16 GB of VRAM. Additional hardware features include 472 GB of bundled local SSD storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

The hardware profile exhibits distinct performance characteristics driven by its GPU acceleration alongside modest general CPU capabilities. Standard CPU benchmarks show limited raw host compute throughput, with stress-ng single-core (952.78) and multi-core (2375.81) scores falling into lower benchmark percentiles, alongside modest memory bandwidth of 19.43 GB/sec uncached read. However, offloading tasks to the NVIDIA P100 GPU yields strong performance in targeted operations. In LLM prompt processing, the server delivers top-tier throughput of 9863.53 tokens/sec on 135M models and 316.25 tokens/sec on 7B models, with text generation reaching 42.76 tokens/sec on 7B models.

Considering its hardware composition, the ecs.gn5-c4g1.xlarge offers specialized cost efficiency for workloads that offload heavy execution to the dedicated GPU rather than relying primarily on host CPU compute. The balance of 30 GB system memory and 16 GB VRAM allows moderate model sizes and dataset batches to reside locally alongside 472 GB of attached SSD storage. It is best suited for deep learning inference, machine learning model evaluation, computer vision processing, and moderate-scale large language model prompt processing.
